text: {"score":3,"justification":"Numbers match the card and the tool outputs, and the 'inconclusive' leaning and cautious next steps are reasonable. But the headline 'Random charts support billing (1 of 30 below billed)' leans toward exoneration while the body says the evidence is too thin, and only 5 of the 99215s were documented. The summary also names C0073157, a 99214 claim, as a target for 99215 chart requests. It cites only low-complexity examples and none of the high-complexity ones. It does not use the by-complexity table, which shows 99215 share rising with complexity and so partly supports a sicker panel. The next steps are generic, without a concrete claim list or a request for the missing results/audit trail.","problems":["Headline implies charts support billing, which conflicts with the 'inconclusive / too few documented 99215s' conclusion.","Next step lists C0073157 (a 99214 claim) as a 99215 chart request; it is a mismatch.","Examples cited are all low-complexity or the single below-billed claim; no high-complexity 99215 claims or documented supported ones (e.g., C0073255 at 45 min) are shown, so the picture is one-sided.","Does not use the complexity gradient (7% to 73% 99215 share), which is relevant to the sicker-panel question.","Does not follow up on the MISSING_RESULTS deficiency; 'no audit trail was received' is noted but no request is made.","Claims that 24% of 99215s were low-complexity without noting the peer baseline, and 'no note inflation signals' is slightly stronger than the evidence given the 17% problems rate.","Next steps are generic; they do not specify the sample size or selection method."]}
